newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin son-in-law elected Aeroflot head.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin son-in-law elected Aeroflot head.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's son-in-law was elected chief executive of Russia's flagship airline Aeroflot on Friday, a company spokesman said.

Valery Okulov, who is married to Yeltsin's eldest daughter, Yelena, had been named acting head of the company by Aeroflot's board of directors in March. He had been deputy head of the airline before Yeltsin appointed the company's previous chief, Yevgeny Shaposhnikov, a former Soviet defence minister, to his Kremlin staff.
"Okulov was elected by 92.7 percent of Aeroflot shareholders," the spokesman said after the company's annual shareholders' meeting.

A new nine-member board of directors of the company was also elected. Among those named were Gennady Zaitsev, head of Federal Aviation Service, as chairman of the board, Shaposhnikov and Andrei Petrov, a deputy finance minister, the spokesman said.
The state owns 51 percent of Aeroflot's shares. Its 14,000 employees hold the rest.

Okulov, 45, flew as a pilot navigator on Aeroflot airliners for 20 years before entering the top management in June 1996. He and Yelena have a teenage daughter and a son, also named Boris Yeltsin, who entered a private school in England last year.
There was no indication Yeltsin, 66, played any part in Okulov's elevation.
